title: Butane camp stove safety
summary: Outdoor use only for the stoves I checked: ventilation, pot size, canister heat limits, leaks and storage.

sources.title: Eureka! SPRK+ camp stove instruction manual (model 2572201)
Iwatani Cassette Feu ZA-3HP portable butane stove instruction manual
Singapore Consumer Product Safety Office: Safety tips on portable butane stoves and gas canisters

blocks.text: **Most portable butane stoves are made for outdoor use only.** They make carbon monoxide (CO), which has no smell and can kill. The two manuals checked for this guide (Eureka SPRK+, Iwatani ZA-3HP) both say never to use it in a home, tent, car, camper or apartment. **Read the label on your own stove.** If it says outdoor use only, use it outside.

Iwatani's manual allows indoor use only in a restaurant with a properly equipped ventilation hood. Consumer Product Safety Commission advice is the same: don't use portable fuel-burning camping equipment inside unless it is designed for enclosed spaces.

items: Put the stove on a flat, stable, heat-resistant surface, outdoors, out of the wind.
Keep it at least **3 feet** from anything that burns (Eureka). Iwatani asks for 6 inches at the sides and back and 36 inches above.
Check the control is **OFF**. Lock the canister in. Only use the fuel the stove maker names.
Light it. **Never leave a lit stove unattended.**
**Never use a pan or griddle that sits over the canister compartment.** It bounces heat back onto the canister, which can overheat and explode.
Eureka SPRK+: no pan wider than **11 inches**. Iwatani ZA-3HP: the bottom of the pot should be under **9.5 inches** and shouldn't touch the canister cover. Your stove may differ.
Don't put two stoves side by side or one pan across two stoves.
No aluminum foil on the grate, no ceramic cookware, don't heat an empty pan.
Don't use it as a heater. Don't use it to start charcoal.
Don't use it in strong wind: the flame can blow out and gas keeps flowing.
Keep canisters upright. Avoid hard knocks.
Keep them out of the sun and away from heat. Don't store above **120°F** (Eureka). Iwatani says keep canisters under **104°F** (40°C).
Iwatani says not to use its stove below **32°F**. Eureka's troubleshooting says to check that it is above 32°F if no gas comes out.
**Remove the canister after every use**, once the stove has cooled for 10 to 15 minutes. Cap it.
Don't use a canister stored many years (Iwatani: more than 6 or 7 years as a rough guide). Don't use deformed canisters. Check rusty ones for leaks and use them up soon.
Never put a canister in a fire. Empty ones go out as your city's rules say.
Store canisters outdoors in a ventilated place, not inside a building or garage (Eureka). If your stove is stored indoors, take the canister out first.
Brush soapy water on the joint where the canister meets the stove.
**Bubbles mean a leak.** Don't use the stove. **Never check with a flame.**

blocks.text: **If you smell gas:** don't light anything. Put out all flames. Turn the stove off and remove the canister. Open a window or door. Iwatani says don't use a ventilating fan. Wait 5 minutes before relighting. Butane is heavier than air and sinks to the floor. If the smell is strong, leave the building.
If the flame is yellow or odd

A good flame is blue with a hint of yellow at the tip. A big yellow flame, a red flame, strange noises or a strange smell: turn it off, remove the canister, and see your manual's troubleshooting section.
Cold, heat, wind and altitude can all make a butane stove work poorly. Don't force it.
